question_english: Can the plane be tiled with any quadrilateral? Describe a method. Why can't a regular pentagon tile the plane?
question_hinglish: Kya kisi bhi quadrilateral se plane ko tile kar sakte hain? Ek tareeka batao. Regular pentagon se plane tile kyun nahi hota?
answer_english:
Yes, the plane can be tiled with any given 4-gon (even a non-convex one). At every vertex of a tiling the angles must add up to 360°, and a quadrilateral's four angles add up to exactly 360°, so 4 copies can fit around a point using each angle once.
Method 1: rotate a copy by 180° about the midpoint of one of its edges; it fits perfectly along that edge. Repeating this at every edge of every copy tiles the plane.
Method 2: draw the grid of Varignon parallelograms of the quadrilateral, place copies on alternate parallelograms, and the gaps form further copies automatically.
A regular pentagon has interior angles of 108°, and 360° is not a whole-number multiple of 108°, so copies cannot fit around a vertex without gaps or overlaps.
answer_hinglish:

Tareeka 1: ek copy ko uski kisi edge ke midpoint ke chaaron taraf 180° ghumaao; ye us edge pe bilkul fit hoti hai. Har copy ki har edge pe ye doharaane se plane tile ho jaata hai.
Tareeka 2: quadrilateral ke Varignon parallelograms ka grid banao, ek-chhod-ek parallelograms pe copies rakho, aur khaali jagah apne aap aur copies ban jaati hain.
Regular pentagon ke andar ke angles 108° hain, aur 360°, 108° ka poora multiple nahi, toh copies vertex ke chaaron taraf bina gap ya overlap ke fit nahi hoti.

question_english: What are aperiodic tilings? Why are they important, and what was discovered in 2023?
question_hinglish: Aperiodic tilings kya hain? Ye kyun mahatvapoorn hain, aur 2023 mein kya khoja gaya?
answer_english: An aperiodic tiling covers the plane endlessly without ever exactly repeating the same pattern. Such tilings turned out to describe the atomic arrangements of quasicrystals, discovered by Dan Shechtman, which were thought to be physically impossible; he won the 2011 Chemistry Nobel Prize. In 2023, Smith, Myers, Kaplan and Goodman-Strauss discovered the 'hat', the first single shape that tiles the plane only aperiodically.
answer_hinglish: Aperiodic tiling plane ko anant tak dhakti hai par kabhi bilkul same pattern nahi doharaati. Aisi tilings quasicrystals ki atomic vyavastha batane mein kaam aayi, jinhe Dan Shechtman ne khoja tha aur jo pehle physically namumkin maane jaate the; unhe 2011 ka Chemistry Nobel mila. 2023 mein Smith, Myers, Kaplan aur Goodman-Strauss ne 'hat' khoja, pehla akela shape jo plane ko sirf aperiodically tile karta hai.
ncert_context: Mathematicians have found many interesting ways to tile the plane using a small set of shapes. Some of these, called aperiodic tilings, turned out to be useful to describe atomic arrangements of quasicrystals — new physical structures that were discovered some time later. The discovery of quasicrystals, made by Dan Shechtman, was very surprising because the atomic arrangement was outside what was then considered physically possible. Dan Shechtman won the chemistry Nobel prize in 2011 for his discovery. The following shape — the first of its kind! — that leads to aperiodic tilings was discovered only recently in 2023 by a team of four mathematicians (Smith, Myers, Kaplan and Goodman-Strauss). You will find that the hat shape will tile the plane endlessly, but without ever quite repeating the same pattern. That is why it is called an 'aperiodic' tiling.

question_english: (a) A 4-gon has sides 2, 5 and 11. Can the fourth side be 100, 10 or 1? What lengths are possible? (b) How many diagonals does an n-gon have? (c) What is the sum of the angles of an n-gon?
question_hinglish: (a) Ek 4-gon ki sides 2, 5 aur 11 hain. Kya chauthi side 100, 10 ya 1 ho sakti hai? Kaun si lambaaiyan sambhav hain? (b) n-gon ke kitne diagonals hote hain? (c) n-gon ke angles ka jod kya hai?
answer_english:
(a) A 4-gon exists exactly when the longest side is less than the sum of the other three.
100: 2 + 5 + 11 = 18 < 100, so no.
10: the longest is 11 < 2 + 5 + 10 = 17, so yes.
1: 11 > 2 + 5 + 1 = 8, so no.
Possible fourth side x: 4 < x < 18.
(b) Each vertex joins to n − 3 non-adjacent vertices, and each diagonal is counted twice: n(n − 3)/2. So 4-gon 2, 5-gon 5, 6-gon 9, 7-gon 14, 8-gon 20.
(c) An n-gon can be cut into n − 2 triangles, so the angle sum is (n − 2) × 180° (180° for a triangle, 360° for a 4-gon, 540° for a 5-gon).
answer_hinglish:
(a) 4-gon tabhi banta hai jab sabse lambi side baaki teen ke jod se kam ho.
100: 2 + 5 + 11 = 18 < 100, toh nahi.
10: sabse lambi 11 < 2 + 5 + 10 = 17, toh haan.
1: 11 > 2 + 5 + 1 = 8, toh nahi.
Sambhav chauthi side x: 4 < x < 18.
(b) Har vertex n − 3 non-adjacent vertices se judta hai, aur har diagonal do baar gina jaata hai: n(n − 3)/2. Toh 4-gon 2, 5-gon 5, 6-gon 9, 7-gon 14, 8-gon 20.
(c) n-gon ko n − 2 triangles mein kaat sakte hain, toh angles ka jod (n − 2) × 180° hai (triangle 180°, 4-gon 360°, 5-gon 540°).

question_english: In ΔABC, P is on AB and the line through P parallel to BC meets AC at Q. If AP = 1, PB = 2 and AQ = 5, find QC. How can the Midpoint Theorem idea be used to trisect a segment?
question_hinglish: ΔABC mein P, AB pe hai aur P se BC ke parallel line AC ko Q pe kaatti hai. Agar AP = 1, PB = 2 aur AQ = 5, toh QC nikaalo. Midpoint Theorem ke idea se segment ko teen barabar hisson mein kaise baantein?
answer_english:
Divide AB into three equal parts of length 1 (AP and two parts of PB) and draw lines through the division points parallel to BC. By repeatedly applying the converse of the Midpoint Theorem, these lines cut AC into three equal parts too, each equal to AQ = 5. So QC = 2 × 5 = 10, and AP/PB = AQ/QC = 1/2.
Trisection: in parallelogram ABCD with M, N the midpoints of AB and CD, the segments DM and BN trisect the diagonal AC. So to trisect PQ, build a parallelogram with PQ as a diagonal and join a pair of opposite vertices to the midpoints of the opposite sides. (The centroid's 2 : 1 division also gives a trisection method.)
answer_hinglish:
AB ko 1-1 ke teen barabar hisson (AP aur PB ke do hisse) mein baanto aur baantne ke points se BC ke parallel lines kheecho. Midpoint Theorem ke converse ko baar-baar lagaane se ye lines AC ko bhi teen barabar hisson mein kaatti hain, har ek AQ = 5 ke barabar. Toh QC = 2 × 5 = 10, aur AP/PB = AQ/QC = 1/2.
Trisection: parallelogram ABCD mein M, N, AB aur CD ke midpoints hon, toh DM aur BN diagonal AC ko teen barabar hisson mein baantte hain. Toh PQ ko trisect karne ke liye PQ ko diagonal maankar parallelogram banao aur opposite vertices ki ek jodi ko saamne ki sides ke midpoints se jodo. (Centroid ka 2 : 1 bantwaara bhi trisection ka tareeka deta hai.)

subject: Mathematics
question_english: Show that the angle sum of a self-intersecting quadrilateral ABCD (with AB and CD crossing at E) is less than 360°.
question_hinglish: Dikhaao ki self-intersecting quadrilateral ABCD (jisme AB aur CD, E pe kaatti hain) ke angles ka jod 360° se kam hai.
answer_english: The crossing point E splits the figure into two triangles, ΔEAD and ΔEBC, which have vertically opposite angles at E. In ΔEAD, ∠A + ∠D = 180° − ∠AED; in ΔEBC, ∠B + ∠C = 180° − ∠BEC. Adding, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 360° − (∠AED + ∠BEC) < 360°, since the angles at E are positive. By making the angles at E close to 180° (a very flat crossing), the sum can be made as small as we like, e.g. 2°.
answer_hinglish: Katne ka point E figure ko do triangles ΔEAD aur ΔEBC mein baantta hai, jinke E pe vertically opposite angles hain. ΔEAD mein ∠A + ∠D = 180° − ∠AED; ΔEBC mein ∠B + ∠C = 180° − ∠BEC. Jodne pe ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 360° − (∠AED + ∠BEC) < 360°, kyunki E pe angles positive hain. E pe angles ko 180° ke paas (bahut chapta kaatna) karke jod ko jitna chaaho chhota kar sakte hain, jaise 2°.
ncert_context: Third, do we want to call CUTS a quadrilateral? Ordinarily, CUTS is not considered a quadrilateral. If we want to include it, we call it a self-intersecting quadrilateral. You know that the sum of angles of a quadrilateral is 360°, even for a non-convex quadrilateral. Now consider a self-intersecting quadrilateral ABCD, where AB and CD intersect at point E. Show that ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D < 360°. Can you construct ABCD such that ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 2°? The sum of the angles of a triangle is 180°.

question_english: What is a linear equation in two variables? What is its standard form? Express Radha's purchase (mangoes ₹60/kg, bananas ₹50/kg, total ₹280) as one.
question_hinglish: Do variables waali linear equation kya hai? Iska standard form kya hai? Radha ki khareedaari (aam ₹60/kg, kela ₹50/kg, kul ₹280) ko aisi equation mein likho.
answer_english:
Any equation that can be written as ax + by + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a and b are not both zero, is a linear equation in two variables. ax + by + c = 0 is its standard form: a and b are the coefficients of x and y, and c is the constant.
Radha: let x = kg of mangoes and y = kg of bananas. Cost 60x + 50y = 280, i.e. 60x + 50y − 280 = 0.
Notes: a, b, c may be fractions (multiply to clear them), and ax + c = 0 is a special case (b = 0), e.g. 7 + 4x = 0 is 4x + 0·y + 7 = 0.
answer_hinglish:
Jo bhi equation ax + by + c = 0 roop mein likhi ja sake, jahan a, b, c real numbers hain aur a aur b dono zero nahi, woh do variables waali linear equation hai. ax + by + c = 0 iska standard form hai: a aur b, x aur y ke coefficients, aur c constant hai.
Radha: x = aam ke kg aur y = kele ke kg. Kharcha 60x + 50y = 280, yaani 60x + 50y − 280 = 0.
Dhyaan do: a, b, c fractions ho sakte hain (guna karke hata do), aur ax + c = 0 ek special case hai (b = 0), jaise 7 + 4x = 0 matlab 4x + 0·y + 7 = 0.

The equation 60x + 50y = 280 is a linear equation in two variables. Any equation that can be expressed in the form ax + by + c = 0, where a, b and c are real numbers, and a and b are not both zero, is called a linear equation in two variables. ax + by + c = 0 is referred to as the standard form of the linear equation. Here a and b are the coefficients of the variables x and y respectively and c is a constant. The coefficients can also be rational numbers; we often multiply the equation by a suitable number to remove the fractions. Equations of the type ax + c = 0 are special cases. For example, 7 + 4x = 0 can be written as 4x + 0×y + 7 = 0.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: What is a solution of a linear equation in two variables? Why is it an ordered pair? How many solutions does such an equation have?
question_hinglish: Do variables waali linear equation ka solution kya hai? Ye ordered pair kyun hai? Aisi equation ke kitne solutions hote hain?
answer_english:
A solution is a pair of values of x and y that satisfies the equation. For 3x + 2y = 12, x = 2, y = 3 is a solution since 3(2) + 2(3) = 12. It is written (2, 3): an ordered pair, since the first number is x and the second y, so order matters. (4, 0) is also a solution, but (1, 3) is not (3 + 6 = 9 ≠ 12).
There are infinitely many solutions: for any value u of x, substituting gives a linear equation in y that can be solved for v, so (u, v) is a solution. E.g. (0, 6), (1, 9/2), (1/2, 21/4) also solve 3x + 2y = 12, but (4, 1) does not.
answer_hinglish:

question_english: Show that 3x + 4y = 7 and 6x + 8y = 14 have the same solutions. In general, why do ax + by = c and kax + kby = kc (k ≠ 0) have the same set of solutions?
question_hinglish: Dikhaao ki 3x + 4y = 7 aur 6x + 8y = 14 ke solutions same hain. Aam taur pe ax + by = c aur kax + kby = kc (k ≠ 0) ke solutions same kyun hote hain?
answer_english:
6x + 8y = 14 is 2 × (3x + 4y = 7). If (x, y) satisfies 3x + 4y = 7, multiplying by 2 shows it satisfies 6x + 8y = 14; dividing by 2 shows the reverse. So both have exactly the same solutions and the same graph.
In general, if ax + by = c then multiplying by k gives kax + kby = kc; and since k ≠ 0, dividing kax + kby = kc by k gives back ax + by = c. So the solution sets are identical.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: What is the slope (gradient) of a line? Define rise and run and give the slope formula.
question_hinglish: Line ka slope (gradient) kya hai? Rise aur run define karo aur slope ka formula do.
answer_english:
Slope measures the steepness of a line. A positive slope means the line goes upward from left to right; a negative slope means it goes downward.
For points A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂) on a line:
Run = x₂ − x₁ (horizontal distance; positive to the right, negative to the left)
Rise = y₂ − y₁ (vertical distance; positive up, negative down)
Slope = Rise/Run = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁)
E.g. through A(2, 0) and B(4, 3): slope = 3/2. The slope is the same whichever two points of the line we use, and in whichever order.
answer_hinglish:
Slope line ki dhalaan (steepness) naapta hai. Positive slope matlab line left se right upar jaati hai; negative slope matlab neeche jaati hai.
Line ke points A(x₁, y₁) aur B(x₂, y₂) ke liye:
Run = x₂ − x₁ (horizontal doori; right positive, left negative)
Rise = y₂ − y₁ (vertical doori; upar positive, neeche negative)
Slope = Rise/Run = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁)
Jaise A(2, 0) aur B(4, 3) se: slope = 3/2. Line ke koi bhi do points kisi bhi kram mein lo, slope same rehta hai.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: What is the slope-intercept form y = mx + d? Prove that m is the slope, and convert ax + by + c = 0 to this form.
question_hinglish: Slope-intercept form y = mx + d kya hai? Siddh karo ki m slope hai, aur ax + by + c = 0 ko is roop mein badlo.
answer_english:
In y = mx + d, m is the slope and d is the y-intercept: the line cuts the y-axis at (0, d).
Proof: take any two points (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂) on the line. Then y₁ = mx₁ + d and y₂ = mx₂ + d, so
(y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = (mx₂ − mx₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = m(x₂ − x₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = m.
So the slope is m for any two points.
From ax + by + c = 0 with b ≠ 0: y = −(a/b)x − c/b, so m = −a/b and d = −c/b.
E.g. 5x + y = 3 → y = −5x + 3: slope −5 (y drops 5 for each unit increase in x), crossing the y-axis at (0, 3).

subject: Mathematics
question_english: Describe the four cases of slope with examples: positive, negative, zero and undefined.
question_hinglish: Slope ke chaar cases examples ke saath batao: positive, negative, zero aur undefined.
answer_english:
1. Positive slope (m > 0): the line rises from left to right; as x increases, y increases. E.g. y = 2x + 1: up 2 for each unit right.
2. Negative slope (m < 0): the line falls from left to right. E.g. y = −3x + 4: down 3 for each unit right.
3. Zero slope (m = 0): a horizontal line parallel to the x-axis; y stays constant. E.g. y = 5.
4. Undefined slope: a vertical line parallel to the y-axis; x stays constant, e.g. x = 2. The run is 0, and division by 0 is undefined. Such a line cannot be written as y = mx + d.
answer_hinglish:
1. Positive slope (m > 0): line left se right upar jaati hai; x badhne pe y badhta hai. Jaise y = 2x + 1: har unit right pe 2 upar.
2. Negative slope (m < 0): line left se right neeche jaati hai. Jaise y = −3x + 4: har unit right pe 3 neeche.
3. Zero slope (m = 0): x-axis ke parallel horizontal line; y same rehta hai. Jaise y = 5.
4. Undefined slope: y-axis ke parallel vertical line; x same rehta hai, jaise x = 2. Run 0 hai, aur 0 se bhaag undefined hai. Aisi line y = mx + d roop mein nahi likhi ja sakti.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: (a) A loading-dock ramp rises 2.5 m over a run of 4 m. Find its slope. (b) A wheelchair ramp must have a slope of 1 cm rise per 12 cm horizontal. How long must it be for stairs 18 cm high?
question_hinglish: (a) Loading-dock ka ramp 4 m ke run pe 2.5 m uthta hai. Slope nikaalo. (b) Wheelchair ramp ka slope 12 cm horizontal pe 1 cm uthaan hona chahiye. 18 cm oonchi seedhiyon ke liye ramp kitna lamba hona chahiye?
answer_english:
(a) Slope = rise/run = 2.5/4 = 0.625 = 5/8.
(b) Horizontal length = 18 × 12 = 216 cm (2.16 m), so that rise/run = 18/216 = 1/12.

question_english: A tank's water level y (cm) after x minutes follows y = 3x. (i) Find the slope and y-intercept and their meaning. (ii) How high is the water after 5 minutes? (iii) When will it reach 21 cm? (iv) Is (4, 10) on the line? (v) Where does it meet x = 3?

subject: Mathematics
question_english: Explain the substitution method by solving 7x − 15y = 2 and x + 2y = 3.
question_hinglish: 7x − 15y = 2 aur x + 2y = 3 hal karke substitution method samjhao.
answer_english:
Step 1: express one variable in terms of the other from either equation: from x + 2y = 3, x = 3 − 2y.
Step 2: substitute into the other equation: 7(3 − 2y) − 15y = 2 → 21 − 29y = 2 → y = 19/29.
Step 3: substitute back: x = 3 − 2(19/29) = 49/29.
Solution: x = 49/29, y = 19/29. Verify by substituting into both equations. Expressing y in terms of x instead gives the same solution.

question_english: Explain the elimination method using: the incomes of two people are in the ratio 9 : 7 and their expenditures 4 : 3, and each saves ₹2000 per month. Find their incomes.
question_hinglish: Elimination method samjhao: do logon ki aay ka ratio 9 : 7 aur kharche ka 4 : 3 hai, aur har ek mahine mein ₹2000 bachaata hai. Unki aay nikaalo.

Let incomes be 9x and 7x, and expenditures 4y and 3y. Savings: 9x − 4y = 2000 …(1) and 7x − 3y = 2000 …(2).

Incomes: 9 × 2000 = ₹18,000 and 7 × 2000 = ₹14,000.
Jaanch: expenditures 16000 : 12000 = 4 : 3.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: (a) Two angles of a triangle are x° and y° with y = 4x, and the third is 50°. Find the angles. (b) The sum of a two-digit number and its reverse is 66 and the digits differ by 2. Find the number(s).
question_hinglish: (a) Triangle ke do angles x° aur y° hain jahan y = 4x, aur teesra 50° hai. Angles nikaalo. (b) Do-ank number aur uske ulte ka jod 66 hai aur ankon ka fark 2 hai. Number(s) nikaalo.
answer_english:
(a) x + y + 50 = 180 and y = 4x → 5x = 130 → x = 26°, y = 104°.
(b) Tens digit x, units y: (10x + y) + (10y + x) = 66 → x + y = 6. Digits differ by 2: taking x > y, x − y = 2. Adding: x = 4, y = 2, so the number is 42. If the units digit is the larger one, the number is 24. Both 42 and 24 satisfy the conditions (42 + 24 = 66).
answer_hinglish:
(a) x + y + 50 = 180 aur y = 4x → 5x = 130 → x = 26°, y = 104°.
(b) Dahaai ka ank x, ikaai y: (10x + y) + (10y + x) = 66 → x + y = 6. Ankon ka fark 2: x > y lekar x − y = 2. Jodne pe x = 4, y = 2, toh number 42 hai. Agar ikaai ka ank bada ho, toh number 24 hai. 42 aur 24 dono shartein poori karte hain (42 + 24 = 66).
ncert_context: Example 8: If two angles of a triangle are x° and y° with y = 4x, and the third angle is 50°, what are the angles? Using the angle sum property of triangles, x° + y° + 50° = 180° (1). If the digits of the number differ by 2, find the number. How many such numbers are there? Let the ten's and the unit's digits in the first number be x and y, respectively. Also let us assume that x is the larger digit. (10x + y) + (10y + x) = 66. Thus 11(x + y) = 66, i.e., x + y = 6 (1). x – y = 2 (2). Solving (1) and (2) by elimination, we get x = 4 and y = 2, so, the two-digit number is 42. The number 42 and its reverse 24 when added gives 66.

question_english: Can a pair of linear equations have no solution or infinitely many? Give the ratio rules for a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0.
question_hinglish: Kya linear equations ki jodi ka koi solution na ho ya anginat hon, aisa ho sakta hai? a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 aur a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 ke ratio rules batao.
answer_english:
Yes.
• x − y = 10 and 10x − 10y = 100: multiplying the first by 10 gives the second, so they are the same equation with infinitely many solutions.
• x − y = 10 and 10x − 10y = 101: the left sides become equal but the right sides (100 vs 101) differ, so no (x, y) satisfies both: no solution.
Rules:
1. a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂ → a unique solution (a variable survives elimination).
2. a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂ → infinitely many solutions (one equation is a multiple of the other).
3. a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂ → no solution.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: How is a pair of linear equations solved graphically? What do intersecting, parallel and coincident lines mean? Solve x + 3y = 6 and 2x − 3y = 12 graphically.
question_hinglish: Linear equations ki jodi graph se kaise hal karte hain? Kaatti, parallel aur coincident lines ka kya matlab hai? x + 3y = 6 aur 2x − 3y = 12 ko graph se hal karo.
answer_english:
Draw both lines (using at least two points each). Solutions are points lying on both lines.
• Lines intersect at one point → a unique solution (that point).
• Lines are parallel → no solution.
• Lines coincide → infinitely many solutions.
x + 3y = 6 passes through (0, 2) and (6, 0); 2x − 3y = 12 passes through (0, −4) and (3, −2). The lines meet at (6, 0), so x = 6, y = 0 is the unique solution. This matches a₁/a₂ = 1/2 ≠ b₁/b₂ = 3/(−3) = −1.
answer_hinglish:
Dono lines banao (har ek ke kam se kam do points se). Solutions woh points hain jo dono lines pe hon.
• Lines ek point pe kaatein → ek unique solution (woh point).

question_english: Solve Mahāvīrāchārya's problem: 9 citrons and 7 wood-apples cost 107; 7 citrons and 9 wood-apples cost 101. What is special about these equations? Use the same trick for 5 pencils + 7 pens = ₹50 and 7 pencils + 5 pens = ₹46.
question_hinglish: Mahāvīrāchārya ka sawaal hal karo: 9 citrons aur 7 wood-apples ki keemat 107; 7 citrons aur 9 wood-apples ki 101. In equations mein kya khaas hai? Yahi tarika 5 pencil + 7 pen = ₹50 aur 7 pencil + 5 pen = ₹46 pe lagao.
answer_english:
9x + 7y = 107 and 7x + 9y = 101: the coefficients are interchanged, so add and subtract.
Adding: 16(x + y) = 208 → x + y = 13. Subtracting: 2(x − y) = 6 → x − y = 3. So x = 8, y = 5: citron 8, wood-apple 5. (From Gaṇita sāra saṅgraha, c. 850 CE.)
Pencils and pens: 5x + 7y = 50, 7x + 5y = 46. Adding: 12(x + y) = 96 → x + y = 8. Subtracting: 2(y − x) = 4 → y − x = 2. Pencil ₹3, pen ₹5.

question_english: (a) Plan A costs ₹50 + ₹0.20/minute and Plan B ₹30 + ₹0.30/minute. When is each cheaper and when are they equal? (b) Jacob's watch reads a minutes past 2; 15 minutes later it reads b minutes past 3, with a = 6b. What time was it at the second look? (c) A father's age equals the sum of his four children's ages; in 20 years the children's sum will be twice his age. Find his age.
question_hinglish: (a) Plan A ₹50 + ₹0.20/minute aur Plan B ₹30 + ₹0.30/minute hai. Kab kaun sasta hai aur kab barabar? (c) Pita ki umar chaar bachchon ki umar ke jod ke barabar hai; 20 saal baad bachchon ka jod uski umar ka do guna hoga. Pita ki umar nikaalo.
answer_english:

(c) Let the father be F and the children's total S = F. In 20 years each child gains 20: S + 80 = 2(F + 20) → F + 80 = 2F + 40 → F = 40 years.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: Given 2x + 3y − 8 = 0, write another equation so that the pair gives (i) intersecting lines, (ii) parallel lines, (iii) coincident lines. Also, how many lines have a given slope, and how many have a given slope and pass through a given point?
question_hinglish: 2x + 3y − 8 = 0 di hai; ek aur equation likho taaki jodi (i) kaatti lines, (ii) parallel lines, (iii) coincident lines de. Saath hi, diye gaye slope ki kitni lines hoti hain, aur diye gaye slope aur point se guzarne waali kitni?
answer_english:
(i) Intersecting: change the ratio a : b, e.g. 3x − 2y − 7 = 0 (2/3 ≠ 3/(−2)).
(ii) Parallel: same a : b, different c, e.g. 4x + 6y − 12 = 0 (2/4 = 3/6 ≠ −8/−12).
(iii) Coincident: a multiple of the equation, e.g. 4x + 6y − 16 = 0.
Lines with a given slope m: infinitely many, y = mx + d for every d, all parallel. With a given slope through a given point: exactly one, since d is then fixed.
answer_hinglish:
(i) Kaatti: a : b ka ratio badlo, jaise 3x − 2y − 7 = 0 (2/3 ≠ 3/(−2)).

subject: Mathematics
question_english: What is the history of solving systems of linear equations?
question_hinglish: Linear equations ke systems hal karne ka itihaas kya hai?
answer_english: The earliest traces are in Babylonian cuneiform tablets (c. 2000 BCE). The Chinese Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art (about two thousand years ago) has a whole chapter, fangcheng, solving systems by arranging coefficients in columns of counting rods and combining columns to cancel variables, essentially modern elimination, eighteen centuries before Gauss's name was attached to it. Indian mathematicians including Āryabhaṭa (499 CE) and Brahmagupta (628 CE) also studied systems in several unknowns using systematic reduction techniques including elimination.
answer_hinglish: Sabse purane nishaan Babylonian cuneiform tablets (c. 2000 BCE) mein hain. Chinese Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art (lagbhag do hazaar saal pehle) mein poora chapter fangcheng hai, jo coefficients ko ginti ki dandiyon ke columns mein rakhkar aur columns milaakar variables hata ke systems hal karta tha, jo lagbhag aaj ka elimination hai, Gauss ke naam judne se athaarah sadi pehle. Āryabhaṭa (499 CE) aur Brahmagupta (628 CE) samet Bharatiya mathematicians ne bhi kai unknowns waale systems ko elimination jaisi vyavasthit reduction techniques se padha.
ncert_context: Solving systems of linear equations is one of the oldest problems in mathematics, going back thousands of years. The earliest traces appear in Babylonian cuneiform tablets (c. 2000 BCE). They were studied systematically in ancient China; the Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art (compiled roughly two thousand years ago) devotes an entire chapter, fangcheng, to systems of linear equations, solved by arranging coefficients in columns of counting rods and then combining columns to cancel out variables — a procedure essentially identical to modern elimination, fully eighteen centuries before Gauss's name became attached to it in Europe. Many Indian mathematicians, including Āryabhaṭa (499 CE) and Brahmagupta (628 CE), also studied general systems of equations in several unknowns using their own systematic reduction techniques including elimination.

chapter: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume
question_english: Give the total surface area and volume of a cuboid and a cube. Why is the volume of a cuboid lwh?
question_hinglish: Cuboid aur cube ka total surface area aur volume batao. Cuboid ka volume lwh kyun hota hai?
answer_english:
A cuboid (a 3D version of a rectangle) has six rectangular faces and dimensions length l, width w, height h.
TSA = 2(wl + hl + hw); Volume V = lwh.
Volume is measured in cubic units: a unit cube has volume 1 cubic unit, and a cuboid's volume is the number of unit cubes that fit in it. Think of it as thin rectangular sheets (area lw) stacked to height h, like a pack of cards, so volume = area of base × height.
Cube of side a (w = h = l): TSA = 6a², V = a³. Cube numbers 1, 8, 27, 64, … are the volumes of cubes of side 1, 2, 3, 4, …
answer_hinglish:
Cuboid (rectangle ka 3D roop) ke chhe rectangular faces aur dimensions lambaai l, chaudaai w, oonchaai h hote hain.
TSA = 2(wl + hl + hw); Volume V = lwh.
Volume cubic units mein naapte hain: unit cube ka volume 1 cubic unit, aur cuboid ka volume usme fit hone waale unit cubes ki sankhya hai. Ise patli rectangular sheets (area lw) ka h oonchaai tak dher socho, cards ki gaddi jaisa, toh volume = base ka area × oonchaai.
a bhuja ka cube (w = h = l): TSA = 6a², V = a³. Cube numbers 1, 8, 27, 64, … bhuja 1, 2, 3, 4, … waale cubes ke volume hain.

chapter: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume
question_english: Cube A has side 6 cm and cuboid B is 9 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm. Compare their volumes and surface areas. Why does this matter in real life?
question_hinglish: Cube A ki bhuja 6 cm aur cuboid B 9 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm hai. Inke volume aur surface area ki tulna karo. Asli zindagi mein ye kyun maayne rakhta hai?
answer_english:
Cube A: V = 6³ = 216 cm³; SA = 6 × 36 = 216 cm².
Cuboid B: V = 9 × 6 × 4 = 216 cm³; SA = 2(54 + 24 + 36) = 228 cm².
Same volume, but the cuboid has the greater surface area. For the same storage capacity, a cube needs less covering material, while a cuboid exposes more area to its surroundings. This matters in packaging, heat transfer and engineering.

ncert_context: Example 1: Two solid objects are made from the same material: Cube A has side 6 cm and Cuboid B has dimensions 9 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm. Compare their volumes and surface areas and determine which object has a greater surface area. For Cube A, its volume is a³ = (6 cm)³ = 216 cm³ and surface area is 6a² = 216 cm². question_english: (a) A 4 cm cube is cut into 1 cm cubes. Compare the total surface areas. Why does this matter in biology? (b) Three faces of a cuboid meeting at a corner have areas 6, 15 and 10 cm². Find its volume.
question_hinglish: (a) 4 cm ke cube ko 1 cm ke cubes mein kaata gaya. Total surface areas ki tulna karo. Biology mein ye kyun maayne rakhta hai? (b) Cuboid ke ek kone pe milne waale teen faces ke area 6, 15 aur 10 cm² hain. Volume nikaalo.
answer_english:
(a) Original: 6 × 16 = 96 cm². There are 4³ = 64 small cubes, each with 6 cm²: 384 cm². Ratio 96 : 384 = 1 : 4. The volume is unchanged, but cutting into smaller pieces greatly increases the surface area, which has major consequences in the biological world.

question_english: A 5 cm cube painted on all faces is cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have exactly 3, 2, 1 and 0 painted faces? Also, how many unit cubes must be added to a cube of side a to make one of side a + 1?
question_hinglish: Saare faces pe paint kiya 5 cm ka cube 1 cm ke cubes mein kaata gaya. Kitne chhote cubes ke theek 3, 2, 1 aur 0 faces paint hain? Saath hi, a bhuja ke cube ko a + 1 bhuja ka banaane ke liye kitne unit cubes jodne padenge?
answer_english:
Three faces: the 8 corner cubes.

One face: on each of the 6 faces, the inner 3 × 3 = 9 cubes: 54.
None: the inner 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cubes.
Jaanch: 8 + 36 + 54 + 27 = 125 = 5³.
Growing a cube: (a + 1)³ − a³ = 3a² + 3a + 1 unit cubes must be added.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume
question_english: What is a right circular cylinder? Derive its curved surface area, total surface area and volume. What is a cross-section?
question_hinglish: Right circular cylinder kya hai? Iska curved surface area, total surface area aur volume derive karo. Cross-section kya hai?
answer_english:
In a right circular cylinder, the cross-section parallel to the base is a circle ('circular') and the axis is perpendicular to the base ('right'), like many pipes. If the axis is inclined, it is an oblique cylinder.
A cross-section is the shape of an extremely thin slice of a solid; for a cylinder it is a circle when sliced parallel to the base and a rectangle when sliced parallel to the axis (MRI scans view the body in such slices).
CSA: cutting the curved surface and opening it out gives a rectangle of length 2πr and height h, so CSA = 2πrh.
TSA (closed both ends) = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r). Open at one end (like a tumbler) = 2πrh + πr² = πr(2h + r).
Volume = cross-sectional area × height = πr²h, like a stack of thin circular khakhras.
answer_hinglish:
Right circular cylinder mein base ke parallel cross-section circle hota hai ('circular') aur axis base ke perpendicular hota hai ('right'), jaise kai pipes. Axis tirchha ho toh oblique cylinder.
Cross-section kisi solid ki bahut patli phaank ka aakaar hai; cylinder ko base ke parallel kaatne pe circle aur axis ke parallel kaatne pe rectangle milta hai (MRI scans shareer ko aisi phaankon mein dekhte hain).
CSA: curved surface ko kaatkar kholne pe 2πr lambaai aur h oonchaai ka rectangle milta hai, toh CSA = 2πrh.
TSA (dono sire band) = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r). Ek sira khula (glass jaisa) = 2πrh + πr² = πr(2h + r).
Volume = cross-section ka area × oonchaai = πr²h, jaise patle gol khakhron ka dher.
ncert_context: The term circular indicates that the cross-section of the cylinder is a circle, while the term right signifies that the axis of the cylinder is perpendicular to its circular base. Many pipes have this shape. Some cylinders may have axes that are inclined rather than perpendicular to the base. The second one is an oblique circular cylinder. Given a three-dimensional object, suppose we take an extremely thin slice of it. The shape we get is called a 'cross-section' of the object. In the case of a cylinder, if the slice is parallel to its base, we get a circular cross-section. If the slice is parallel to the axis, we get a rectangular cross-section. When doctors take an MRI scan, it is like taking a cross-section. Suppose the cylinder is cut. We get a rectangle. The curved surface area (CSA) of the cylinder is CSA = circumference × height = 2πrh. Total surface area (TSA) = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r). If the cylinder is closed at one end and open at the other end, like a tumbler, then surface area = 2πrh + πr² = πr(2h + r). The volume V of the cylinder is V = cross-sectional area × height = πr²h. Think of the cylinder as a large number of thin circular khakhras stacked on one another.

The term circular indicates that the cross-section of the cylinder is a circle, while the term right signifies that the axis of the cylinder is perpendicular to its circular base. Many pipes have this shape. Some cylinders may have axes that are inclined rather than perpendicular to the base. The second one is an oblique circular cylinder. Given a three-dimensional object, suppose we take an extremely thin slice of it. The shape we get is called a 'cross-section' of the object. In the case of a cylinder, if the slice is parallel to its base, we get a circular cross-section. If the slice is parallel to the axis, we get a rectangular cross-section. When doctors take an MRI scan, it is like taking a cross-section. Suppose the cylinder is cut. We get a rectangle. The curved surface area (CSA) of the cylinder is CSA = circumference × height = 2πrh. Total surface area (TSA) = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r). If the cylinder is closed at one end and open at the other end, like a tumbler, then surface area = 2πrh + πr² = πr(2h + r). The volume V of the cylinder is V = cross-sectional area × height = πr²h. Think of the cylinder as a large number of thin circular khakhras stacked on one another.

chapter: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume
question_english: How is a right circular cone formed? Derive its curved surface area and give its total surface area.
question_hinglish: Right circular cone kaise banta hai? Iska curved surface area derive karo aur total surface area batao.
answer_english:
A right circular cone is generated by rotating a right triangle about one of its legs. Slant height l, height h and radius r satisfy l² = h² + r² (Baudhāyana–Pythagoras).
CSA: cut along a slant edge and unroll; the surface is a sector of a circle of radius l. Divide it into many thin sectors, each nearly an isosceles triangle of height l with bases b₁, b₂, …: CSA = ½(b₁ + b₂ + …)l = ½ × 2πr × l = πrl.
Alternatively, the sector's area is πl² × θ/360 and its arc 2πl × θ/360 equals the base circumference 2πr, so θ/360 = r/l and CSA = πrl.
TSA = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r).
answer_hinglish:
Right circular cone ek right triangle ko uski ek bhuja ke chaaron taraf ghumaane se banta hai. Slant height l, oonchaai h aur radius r mein l² = h² + r² (Baudhāyana–Pythagoras).
CSA: slant edge se kaatkar kholo; surface l radius ke circle ka sector ban jaati hai. Ise bahut patle sectors mein baanto, har ek l oonchaai aur b₁, b₂, … base waala lagbhag isosceles triangle: CSA = ½(b₁ + b₂ + …)l = ½ × 2πr × l = πrl.
Ya: sector ka area πl² × θ/360 aur arc 2πl × θ/360, base ki circumference 2πr ke barabar hai, toh θ/360 = r/l aur CSA = πrl.
TSA = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r).
ncert_context: A right circular cone is generated when a right triangle is rotated about one of its legs. The relationship among the slant length l, the height h, the radius r of the base is l² = h² + r² (using the Baudhāyana–Pythagoras theorem). Imagine cutting the cone along a slant edge and 'opening up' or unrolling the surface. The unrolled surface has the shape of a sector of a circle. Cutting it up into a large number of very thin sectors, each of which can be regarded as a narrow isosceles triangle of height l. CSA = ½b₁l + ½b₂l + … + ½bₙl = ½ × circumference of the base × l = ½(2πr)l = πrl. From the formula for area of a sector of a circle, CSA = πl² × θ°/360°. From the cone, arc length = s = 2πr, and from the sector, arc length = θ°/360° × 2πl. Equating these two, we get θ°/360° = r/l. The curved surface area is CSA = πrl. The total surface area (TSA) is TSA = πrl + πr².

Answer the question in English using only the given context.

A right circular cone is generated by rotating a right triangle about one of its legs. Slant height l, height h and radius r satisfy l² = h² + r² (Baudhāyana–Pythagoras).
CSA: cut along a slant edge and unroll; the surface is a sector of a circle of radius l. Divide it into many thin sectors, each nearly an isosceles triangle of height l with bases b₁, b₂, …: CSA = ½(b₁ + b₂ + …)l = ½ × 2πr × l = πrl.
Alternatively, the sector's area is πl² × θ/360 and its arc 2πl × θ/360 equals the base circumference 2πr, so θ/360 = r/l and CSA = πrl.
TSA = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r).

question_english: What is the volume of a cone? How can the factor 1/3 be verified experimentally? Who first found it?
question_hinglish: Cone ka volume kya hai? 1/3 factor ko experiment se kaise jaanch sakte hain? Ise sabse pehle kisne khoja?
answer_english:
V = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3) × area of base × height, i.e. one-third of the cylinder with the same base and height. Proving the 1/3 needs calculus (Grade 12), but it can be verified:
• Salt: fill a paper cone (same radius and height as a cylindrical tin) with salt and empty it into the tin. It takes exactly three cone-fulls to fill the cylinder.
• Clay: mould clay into a cylinder, then reshape the same clay into cones of the same radius and height; exactly three cones are made.
The formula was first found by Archimedes (c. 225 BCE), who also found the sphere formulas.

The formula for the volume of a cone was first found by the Greek mathematician Archimedes (c. 225 BCE).

question_english: (a) A right triangle with sides 5, 12, 13 cm is rotated about the 12 cm side. Find the volume of the solid. (b) A 6-8-10 cm right triangle is rotated about the 8 cm side. Find the volume and CSA (π ≈ 22/7).
question_hinglish: (a) 5, 12, 13 cm bhujaon waale right triangle ko 12 cm bhuja ke chaaron taraf ghumaaya gaya. Bane solid ka volume nikaalo. (b) 6-8-10 cm right triangle ko 8 cm bhuja ke chaaron taraf ghumaaya. Volume aur CSA nikaalo (π ≈ 22/7).
answer_english:
(a) 5² + 12² = 13², so the legs are 5 and 12. Rotating about 12 cm gives a cone with h = 12, r = 5.
V = (1/3)π × 25 × 12 = 100π cm³ (≈ 314 cm³).
(b) Cone with h = 8, r = 6, l = 10.
V = (1/3) × 22/7 × 36 × 8 = 96π ≈ 301.7 cm³.
CSA = πrl = 22/7 × 6 × 10 ≈ 188.6 cm² (= 60π).

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume
question_english: What is a pyramidal shape? Give its volume formula and examples. How is its surface area found?
question_hinglish: Pyramidal shape kya hai? Iska volume formula aur examples do. Iska surface area kaise nikaalte hain?
answer_english:
A pyramidal shape has a flat base of any closed shape (triangle, square, …) with every point of the base joined to a single apex in a different plane.
Volume V = (1/3) × area of base × height, for any base shape. This is the same as the cone formula; a cone is a pyramid with a circular base.
Surface area: add up the areas of all the faces; no separate formula is needed.
Examples: the Egyptian pyramids (square bases), Rubik's triangular-base puzzle, and pyramidal mountain peaks formed by glacier erosion, like Shivling Peak in Uttarakhand and the Matterhorn in the Alps.
answer_hinglish:
Pyramidal shape ka ek samtal base kisi bhi band aakaar ka hota hai (triangle, square, …) aur base ka har point doosre plane ke ek apex se juda hota hai.
Volume V = (1/3) × base ka area × oonchaai, kisi bhi base ke liye. Ye cone ke formula jaisa hai; cone gol base waala pyramid hai.
Surface area: saare faces ke area jodo; alag formula nahi chahiye.
Examples: Egypt ke pyramids (square base), Rubik ka triangular base waala puzzle, aur glacier se bane pyramidal pahaadi shikhar, jaise Uttarakhand ka Shivling Peak aur Alps ka Matterhorn.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume
question_english: What is a sphere? How did Archimedes find its surface area? How can 4πr² be verified with a ball and string?
question_hinglish: Sphere kya hai? Archimedes ne iska surface area kaise nikaala? Gend aur dhaage se 4πr² kaise jaanch sakte hain?
answer_english:
A sphere is the set of all points in 3D space at a given distance r (the radius) from a given point O (the centre), the 3D equivalent of a circle. Rotating a circle about a diameter gives a hollow sphere.
Archimedes showed that the surface area of a sphere equals the curved surface area of the cylinder of radius r and height 2r that fits tightly around it: 2πr × 2r = 4πr².
String activity: wind string tightly over a ball until it is covered, then unwind it and use it to fill circles of the ball's radius. It fills exactly 4 circles, so surface area = 4πr².
The sphere–cylinder idea is used in rectangular world maps, which distort shapes near the poles but not near the equator.
answer_hinglish:
Sphere 3D space ke un saare points ka set hai jo ek diye point O (centre) se di gayi doori r (radius) pe hon, circle ka 3D roop. Circle ko diameter ke chaaron taraf ghumaane se khokhla sphere banta hai.
Archimedes ne dikhaaya ki sphere ka surface area usse kas ke lipte r radius aur 2r oonchaai waale cylinder ke curved surface area ke barabar hai: 2πr × 2r = 4πr².
Dhaage ki activity: gend pe dhaaga kas ke lapeto jab tak woh dhak na jaaye, phir kholkar gend ke radius ke circles bharo. Ye theek 4 circles bharta hai, toh surface area = 4πr².
Sphere–cylinder ka idea rectangular world maps mein use hota hai, jo dhruvon ke paas shapes bigaadte hain par equator ke paas nahi.
ncert_context: A sphere is the three-dimensional (3D) equivalent of a circle. Whereas a circle is the collection of all points in a plane that are at some given distance from some given point, a sphere is the collection of all points in 3D space that are at some given distance r (the radius of the sphere) from a given point O, the centre of the sphere. If we rotate the circle about any diameter, we obtain a hollow sphere. Archimedes showed that the surface area A of a sphere with radius r is equal to 4πr². He did this by showing that the surface area of a sphere is exactly equal to the curved surface area of a cylinder with radius r and height h = 2r that fits tightly over the sphere. 2πrh = 2πr × 2r = 4πr². This result is used in cartography, when making a rectangular map projection of the earth. There is great distortion in shapes at high latitudes. Take a rubber ball. Wind a string tightly around the ball. On a sheet of paper, draw four circles with a radius equal to the radius of the ball. Fill the circles with the string. The surface area of a sphere of radius r is equal to 4 times the area of a circle of radius r, i.e., equal to 4πr².

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume
question_english: What is the volume of a sphere? Explain the link with the cone formula using thin cones.
question_hinglish: Sphere ka volume kya hai? Patle cones ki madad se cone ke formula se iska sambandh samjhao.
answer_english:
V = (4/3)πr³ (found by Archimedes).
Link: divide the sphere's surface into many tiny regions and join each to the centre, making many thin cones, all of height r. The sphere's volume is the sum of their volumes:
V = (1/3) × r × (sum of all the tiny base areas) = (1/3) × r × 4πr² = (4/3)πr³.
So volume of sphere = (1/3) × surface area × radius.
answer_hinglish:
V = (4/3)πr³ (Archimedes ne khoja).
Sambandh: sphere ki surface ko bahut chhote hisson mein baanto aur har ek ko centre se jodo, jisse bahut saare patle cones bante hain, sabki oonchaai r. Sphere ka volume unke volumes ka jod hai:
V = (1/3) × r × (saare chhote base areas ka jod) = (1/3) × r × 4πr² = (4/3)πr³.
Toh sphere ka volume = (1/3) × surface area × radius.
ncert_context: Archimedes also found the formula for the volume V of a sphere: V = (4/3)πr³. You will study the derivations of these formulas in later grades, using calculus. But you may be able to find your own derivation of the formula by connecting it with the formula for volume of a cone; namely, by writing it as V = 1/3 × (4πr²) × r, i.e., Volume of sphere = 1/3 × surface area of sphere × radius of sphere. Imagine that the entire surface of the sphere is divided into tiny regions. Now connect all these regions to the centre of the sphere. This creates a large number of thin cones. They all have the same height, namely r. The volume of the sphere is equal to the sum of the volumes of all the cones. Volume of sphere = r/3 × sum of base areas of all the thin cones = r/3 × surface area of sphere = r/3 × 4πr² = (4/3)πr³.

question_hinglish: Hemisphere kya hai? Iska curved surface area, total surface area aur volume examples ke saath batao.
answer_english:
A hemisphere is the solid formed when a sphere is cut into two equal halves by a plane through its centre. It has one curved surface and one flat circular base.

question_english: (a) Two metal spheres weigh 5920 g and 740 g; the smaller has diameter 5 cm. Find the radius of the larger. (b) The moon's diameter is about 1/4 of the earth's. Find the ratio of their surface areas. (c) A sphere's radius increases by 10%; show its volume increases by about 33.1%. (d) If the volume rises by 72.8%, by what % did the radius rise?
question_hinglish: (a) Do metal ke spheres 5920 g aur 740 g ke hain; chhote ka diameter 5 cm hai. Bade ka radius nikaalo. (b) Chaand ka diameter prithvi ka lagbhag 1/4 hai. Surface areas ka ratio nikaalo. (c) Sphere ka radius 10% badhta hai; dikhaao ki volume lagbhag 33.1% badhta hai. (d) Agar volume 72.8% badhe, toh radius kitne % badha?
answer_english:
(a) Same metal, so volumes are in the ratio 5920 : 740 = 8 : 1. Volume ∝ r³, so the radius ratio is ∛8 = 2. The larger radius = 2 × 2.5 = 5 cm.
(b) Surface area ∝ r²: (1/4)² = 1/16, so moon : earth = 1 : 16.
(c) New volume ∝ (1.1r)³ = 1.331r³, an increase of 33.1%.
(d) (1 + x/100)³ = 1.728 = 1.2³ → x = 20%.

question_hinglish: (a) Dikhaao ki sphere ka volume use gherne waale sabse chhote cylinder ka 2/3 hai. (b) Prithvi ki equator pe lipti dorii ko 1 m lambi dorii se badla gaya, jo har jagah barabar oonchaai pe hai. Ye zameen se kitni oonchi hai? Chaand, Jupiter ya volleyball ke liye?
answer_english:

(b) If the radius rises by h, the length rises by 2π(R + h) − 2πR = 2πh. Setting 2πh = 1 m gives h = 1/(2π) ≈ 0.16 m ≈ 16 cm. Surprisingly, this does not depend on R, so it is the same 16 cm for the moon, Jupiter and a volleyball.

question_english: (a) A sphere of radius 5 cm has 5 times the surface area of the curved surface of a cone of radius 4 cm. Find the cone's height and volume. (b) A square pyramid sits inside a cylinder of radius r and height h, with its base corners on the cylinder's base circle and apex on top. Find the ratio of their volumes.
question_hinglish: (a) 5 cm radius ke sphere ka surface area 4 cm radius waale cone ki curved surface ka 5 guna hai. Cone ki oonchaai aur volume nikaalo. answer_english:

question_english: (a) By how much does a cuboid's volume change if its length increases by 1 unit? (b) A cylinder's radius increases by 1 unit? (c) A sphere's radius decreases by 1 unit? (d) Express a cube's surface area S in terms of its volume V, and vice versa.
question_hinglish: (a) Cuboid ki lambaai 1 unit badhne pe volume kitna badalta hai? (b) Cylinder ka radius 1 unit badhne pe? (c) Sphere ka radius 1 unit ghatne pe? (d) Cube ke surface area S ko volume V mein likho, aur ulta.
answer_english:
(a) (l + 1)wh − lwh = wh cubic units.
(b) π(r + 1)²h − πr²h = π(2r + 1)h = 2πrh + πh cubic units.
(c) (4/3)π[r³ − (r − 1)³] = (4/3)π(3r² − 3r + 1) cubic units decrease.
(d) Side a = ∛V, so S = 6a² = 6V^(2/3). Conversely a = √(S/6), so V = (S/6)^(3/2).

chapter: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume
question_english: How many tennis balls of radius 3 cm fit in a 30 ft × 30 ft × 15 ft classroom? Why can't you just divide the room's volume by a ball's volume?
question_hinglish: 30 ft × 30 ft × 15 ft ki class mein 3 cm radius ki kitni tennis balls aayengi? Kamre ke volume ko ball ke volume se seedha bhaag kyun nahi de sakte?
answer_english:
Ball volume = (4/3)π × 27 ≈ 113 cm³. Room ≈ 900 × 900 × 450 cm ≈ 37,80,00,000 cm³ (taking 1 ft ≈ 30 cm).
Dividing gives ≈ 33,45,000, but this is only an upper bound, because spheres cannot fill space without gaps.
Simple stacking (balls in rows, columns and layers): 900/6 = 150 along the length, 150 along the width, 450/6 = 75 along the height: 150 × 150 × 75 = 16,87,500 balls. Other arrangements pack more efficiently and fit more. This is why spheres are not used as units of volume: they leave gaps, unlike cubes.

question_hinglish: (a) Prithvi ka radius 6370 km, Jupiter ka 69,900 km aur Sooraj ka 6,95,700 km lekar Jupiter aur Sooraj ke volume ka Prithvi se ratio nikaalo. (b) Agar Prithvi ka 1.38 billion km³ paani 6371 km radius ke sphere pe ek-samaan parat bane, toh woh lagbhag kitni moti hogi?
answer_english:

(b) For a thin layer, thickness ≈ water volume ÷ surface area = 1.38 × 10⁹ ÷ (4π × 6371²) ≈ 1.38 × 10⁹ ÷ 5.10 × 10⁸ ≈ 2.7 km.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: State the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic. What does 'unique' mean here?
question_hinglish: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic batao. Yahan 'unique' ka kya matlab hai?
answer_english:
Every composite number can be expressed (factorised) as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique, apart from the order in which the prime factors occur.
'Unique' means there is only one way to write the number as a product of primes if we ignore order: 2 × 3 × 5 × 7 is the same as 3 × 5 × 7 × 2. If we always write primes in ascending order, the factorisation is exactly unique, e.g. 32760 = 2³ × 3² × 5 × 7 × 13.

'Unique' ka matlab kram ko nazarandaaz karein toh primes ke guna ka sirf ek hi tareeka hai: 2 × 3 × 5 × 7 aur 3 × 5 × 7 × 2 same hain. Primes ko hamesha badhte kram mein likhein toh factorisation bilkul ek hi hai, jaise 32760 = 2³ × 3² × 5 × 7 × 13.

question_english: How are HCF and LCM found by the prime factorisation method? How are HCF and LCM of two numbers related? Illustrate with 6 and 20.
question_hinglish: Prime factorisation method se HCF aur LCM kaise nikaalte hain? Do numbers ke HCF aur LCM ka kya sambandh hai? 6 aur 20 se dikhaao.
answer_english:
Write each number as a product of prime powers.
HCF = product of the smallest power of each common prime factor.
LCM = product of the greatest power of each prime factor involved.
6 = 2 × 3, 20 = 2² × 5: HCF = 2, LCM = 2² × 3 × 5 = 60.
For any two positive integers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. Check: 2 × 60 = 120 = 6 × 20. This does not hold for three numbers.

HCF = har common prime factor ki sabse chhoti power ka guna.
LCM = har shaamil prime factor ki sabse badi power ka guna.
6 = 2 × 3, 20 = 2² × 5: HCF = 2, LCM = 2² × 3 × 5 = 60.
Kinhi bhi do positive integers a aur b ke liye HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. Jaanch: 2 × 60 = 120 = 6 × 20. Ye teen numbers ke liye sahi nahi hota.

Note that HCF(6, 20) = 2¹ = Product of the smallest power of each common prime factor in the numbers. LCM(6, 20) = 2² × 3¹ × 5¹ = Product of the greatest power of each prime factor, involved in the numbers. You might have noticed that HCF(6, 20) × LCM(6, 20) = 6 × 20. In fact, we can verify that for any two positive integers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. Notice, 6 × 72 × 120 ≠ HCF(6, 72, 120) × LCM(6, 72, 120). So, the product of three numbers is not equal to the product of their HCF and LCM.

question_english: Can 4ⁿ or 6ⁿ end with the digit 0 for any natural number n? Justify using the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic.
question_hinglish: Kya kisi natural number n ke liye 4ⁿ ya 6ⁿ ka aakhri ank 0 ho sakta hai? Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic se samjhao.
answer_english:
A number ending in 0 is divisible by 10 = 2 × 5, so its prime factorisation must contain 5.
4ⁿ = 2²ⁿ: its only prime factor is 2.
6ⁿ = 2ⁿ × 3ⁿ: its only prime factors are 2 and 3.
By the uniqueness in the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, no other prime (in particular 5) can appear. So neither 4ⁿ nor 6ⁿ can ever end with 0.

question_english: Sonia takes 18 minutes and Ravi 12 minutes to drive one round of a circular path. If they start together from the same point in the same direction, after how many minutes will they meet again at the start?

subject: Mathematics
question_english: State and prove Theorem 1.2: if a prime p divides a², then p divides a.
question_hinglish: Theorem 1.2 batao aur siddh karo: agar prime p, a² ko divide kare, toh p, a ko divide karta hai.
answer_english:
Theorem: Let p be a prime. If p divides a², then p divides a (a a positive integer).
Proof: write a = p₁p₂…pₙ (primes, not necessarily distinct). Then a² = p₁²p₂²…pₙ². Since p divides a², by the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic p is one of the prime factors of a². By uniqueness, the only prime factors of a² are p₁, p₂, …, pₙ, so p is one of them. Since a = p₁p₂…pₙ, p divides a.
This result is used to prove that √2, √3, √5 are irrational.
answer_hinglish:

Uniqueness se a² ke prime factors sirf p₁, p₂, …, pₙ hain, toh p inme se ek hai. a = p₁p₂…pₙ hai, toh p, a ko divide karta hai.
Isi result se √2, √3, √5 irrational siddh hote hain.

Therefore, a² = (p₁p₂ . . . pₙ)(p₁p₂ . . . pₙ) = p₁²p₂² . . . pₙ². Now, we are given that p divides a². Therefore, from the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, it follows that p is one of the prime factors of a². However, using the uniqueness part of the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, we realise that the only prime factors of a² are p₁, p₂, . . ., pₙ. So p is one of p₁, p₂, . . ., pₙ. Now, since a = p₁p₂ . . . pₙ, p divides a.

Theorem 1.2: Let p be a prime number. If p divides a², then p divides a, where a is a positive integer. Proof: Let the prime factorisation of a be as follows: a = p₁p₂ . . . pₙ, where p₁, p₂, . . ., pₙ are primes, not necessarily distinct. Therefore, a² = (p₁p₂ . . . pₙ)(p₁p₂ . . . pₙ) = p₁²p₂² . . . pₙ². Now, we are given that p divides a². Therefore, from the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, it follows that p is one of the prime factors of a². However, using the uniqueness part of the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, we realise that the only prime factors of a² are p₁, p₂, . . ., pₙ. So p is one of p₁, p₂, . . ., pₙ. Now, since a = p₁p₂ . . . pₙ, p divides a.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: Prove that √2 is irrational.
question_hinglish: Siddh karo ki √2 irrational hai.
answer_english:
Proof by contradiction. Assume √2 is rational: √2 = a/b with a, b coprime integers, b ≠ 0.
Then b√2 = a; squaring, 2b² = a². So 2 divides a², and by Theorem 1.2, 2 divides a. Let a = 2c.
Then 2b² = 4c², so b² = 2c². So 2 divides b², and hence 2 divides b.
Thus a and b have 2 as a common factor, contradicting that they are coprime. The contradiction arose from assuming √2 is rational, so √2 is irrational.
answer_hinglish:

Tab b√2 = a; square karne pe 2b² = a². Toh 2, a² ko divide karta hai, aur Theorem 1.2 se 2, a ko divide karta hai. a = 2c lo.
Tab 2b² = 4c², toh b² = 2c². Toh 2, b² ko divide karta hai, isliye 2, b ko bhi.
Isliye a aur b ka common factor 2 hai, jo unke coprime hone ke khilaaf hai. Ye virodh √2 ko rational maanne se aaya, toh √2 irrational hai.
ncert_context: The proof is based on a technique called 'proof by contradiction'. Theorem 1.3: √2 is irrational. Proof: Let us assume, to the contrary, that √2 is rational. So, we can find integers r and s (≠ 0) such that √2 = r/s. Suppose r and s have a common factor other than 1. Then, we divide by the common factor to get √2 = a/b, where a and b are coprime. So, b√2 = a. Squaring on both sides and rearranging, we get 2b² = a². Therefore, 2 divides a². Now, by Theorem 1.2, it follows that 2 divides a. So, we can write a = 2c for some integer c. Substituting for a, we get 2b² = 4c², that is, b² = 2c². This means that 2 divides b², and so 2 divides b. Therefore, a and b have at least 2 as a common factor. But this contradicts the fact that a and b have no common factors other than 1. So, we conclude that √2 is irrational.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: Show that 5 − √3 and 3√2 are irrational.
question_hinglish: Dikhaao ki 5 − √3 aur 3√2 irrational hain.
answer_english:
5 − √3: assume it is rational, 5 − √3 = a/b (coprime, b ≠ 0). Then √3 = 5 − a/b = (5b − a)/b. Since a, b are integers, (5b − a)/b is rational, so √3 would be rational, which contradicts that √3 is irrational. So 5 − √3 is irrational.
3√2: assume 3√2 = a/b. Then √2 = a/(3b), which is rational, contradicting that √2 is irrational. So 3√2 is irrational.
These illustrate: rational ± irrational is irrational, and a non-zero rational × irrational is irrational.

question_english: Is HCF × LCM equal to the product for three numbers p, q, r? What formulas hold instead?
question_hinglish: Kya teen numbers p, q, r ke liye HCF × LCM unke guna ke barabar hai? Iski jagah kaun se formulas sahi hain?

subject: Mathematics
question_english: What are the degree of a polynomial and linear, quadratic and cubic polynomials? Give their general forms.
question_hinglish: Polynomial ki degree aur linear, quadratic aur cubic polynomials kya hain? Inke general roop batao.
answer_english:
The degree of a polynomial p(x) is the highest power of x in it.
Linear polynomial (degree 1): ax + b, a ≠ 0, e.g. 2x − 3, 3z + 4.
Quadratic polynomial (degree 2): ax² + bx + c, a ≠ 0, e.g. 2y² − 3y + 4. 'Quadratic' comes from 'quadrate', meaning square.
Cubic polynomial (degree 3): ax³ + bx² + cx + d, a ≠ 0, e.g. 3x³ − 2x² + x − 1.
Expressions like 1/(x − 1) or √x + 2 are not polynomials.

Cubic polynomial (degree 3): ax³ + bx² + cx + d, a ≠ 0, jaise 3x³ − 2x² + x − 1.
1/(x − 1) ya √x + 2 jaise expressions polynomials nahi hain.

question_english: What is the value of a polynomial at x = k, and what is a zero of a polynomial? Find the zeroes of x² − 3x − 4 and of a linear polynomial ax + b.
question_hinglish: x = k pe polynomial ki value kya hai, aur polynomial ka zero kya hai? x² − 3x − 4 aur linear polynomial ax + b ke zeroes nikaalo.
answer_english:
p(k) is the value obtained by replacing x by k in p(x). A real number k is a zero of p(x) if p(k) = 0.
For p(x) = x² − 3x − 4: p(2) = −6, p(0) = −4, p(−1) = 1 + 3 − 4 = 0 and p(4) = 16 − 12 − 4 = 0. So −1 and 4 are its zeroes.
For ax + b: ak + b = 0 gives k = −b/a, i.e. zero = −(constant term)/(coefficient of x). E.g. the zero of 2x + 3 is −3/2.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: What is the geometrical meaning of the zeroes of a polynomial? Explain for linear and quadratic polynomials.
question_hinglish: Polynomial ke zeroes ka geometrical matlab kya hai? Linear aur quadratic polynomials ke liye samjhao.
answer_english:
The zeroes of p(x) are exactly the x-coordinates of the points where the graph of y = p(x) meets the x-axis.
Linear: y = ax + b is a straight line meeting the x-axis at exactly one point (−b/a, 0), so ax + b has exactly one zero. E.g. y = 2x + 3 meets the x-axis at (−3/2, 0).
Quadratic: y = ax² + bx + c is a parabola, opening upward if a > 0 and downward if a < 0. E.g. y = x² − 3x − 4 meets the x-axis at x = −1 and x = 4, its zeroes.
answer_hinglish:
p(x) ke zeroes theek un points ke x-coordinates hain jahan y = p(x) ka graph x-axis ko milta hai.

Quadratic: y = ax² + bx + c ek parabola hai, a > 0 ho toh upar khula, a < 0 ho toh neeche khula. Jaise y = x² − 3x − 4, x-axis ko x = −1 aur x = 4 pe milti hai, jo iske zeroes hain.

The zero of 2x + 3 is –3/2. Thus, the zero of the polynomial 2x + 3 is the x-coordinate of the point where the graph of y = 2x + 3 intersects the x-axis. In general, for a linear polynomial ax + b, a ≠ 0, the graph of y = ax + b is a straight line which intersects the x-axis at exactly one point, namely, (–b/a, 0). For any quadratic polynomial ax² + bx + c, a ≠ 0, the graph of the corresponding equation y = ax² + bx + c has one of the two shapes either open upwards or open downwards depending on whether a > 0 or a < 0. These curves are called parabolas. The zeroes of a quadratic polynomial ax² + bx + c, a ≠ 0, are precisely the x-coordinates of the points where the parabola representing y = ax² + bx + c intersects the x-axis.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: How many zeroes can a quadratic polynomial have? Describe the three cases for the graph of y = ax² + bx + c.
question_hinglish: Quadratic polynomial ke kitne zeroes ho sakte hain? y = ax² + bx + c ke graph ke teen cases batao.
answer_english:
Case (i): the parabola cuts the x-axis at two distinct points A and A′; their x-coordinates are the two distinct zeroes.
Case (ii): it touches the x-axis at exactly one point (two coincident points); the polynomial has two equal zeroes (one zero).
Case (iii): it lies completely above or completely below the x-axis and does not meet it; the polynomial has no (real) zero.
So a quadratic polynomial has at most 2 zeroes.

Case (i): parabola x-axis ko do alag points A aur A′ pe kaatta hai; unke x-coordinates do alag zeroes hain.
Case (ii): ye x-axis ko theek ek point pe chhoota hai (do coincident points); polynomial ke do barabar zeroes (ek zero) hain.
Case (iii): ye poori tarah x-axis ke upar ya neeche hai aur use nahi milta; polynomial ka koi (real) zero nahi.
Toh quadratic polynomial ke zyada se zyada 2 zeroes hote hain.

The x-coordinate of A is the only zero for the quadratic polynomial ax² + bx + c in this case. Case (iii): Here, the graph is either completely above the x-axis or completely below the x-axis. So, it does not cut the x-axis at any point. So, the quadratic polynomial ax² + bx + c has no zero in this case. So, you can see geometrically that a quadratic polynomial can have either two distinct zeroes or two equal zeroes (i.e., one zero), or no zero. subject: Mathematics
question_english: Derive the relationship between the zeroes and coefficients of a quadratic polynomial ax² + bx + c.
question_hinglish: Quadratic polynomial ax² + bx + c ke zeroes aur coefficients ka sambandh derive karo.
answer_english:
If α and β are the zeroes, then (x − α) and (x − β) are factors, so
ax² + bx + c = k(x − α)(x − β) = kx² − k(α + β)x + kαβ for some constant k.
Comparing coefficients: a = k, b = −k(α + β), c = kαβ.
So:
Sum of zeroes α + β = −b/a = −(coefficient of x)/(coefficient of x²)
Product of zeroes αβ = c/a = (constant term)/(coefficient of x²)

question_english: How do you find the number of zeroes of p(x) from the graph of y = p(x)? What can you say if the graph touches the x-axis at one point, or never meets it?
question_hinglish: y = p(x) ke graph se p(x) ke zeroes ki sankhya kaise nikaalte hain? Agar graph x-axis ko ek point pe chhooe, ya kabhi na mile, toh kya kehenge?
answer_english:
Count the points where the graph meets the x-axis: each such point's x-coordinate is a zero.
If the graph meets the x-axis at only one point (crossing it or just touching it), p(x) has exactly one zero (for a quadratic that touches, it is two equal zeroes).
If the graph never meets the x-axis (completely above or below), p(x) has no zeroes.
The number of zeroes can never exceed the degree.

Agar graph x-axis ko kabhi na mile (poora upar ya neeche), toh p(x) ka koi zero nahi.
Zeroes ki sankhya degree se zyada kabhi nahi ho sakti.

question_english: Akhila's Hoopla games are half her Giant Wheel rides. A ride costs ₹3 and a Hoopla game ₹4, and she spent ₹20. Form the equations and find how many rides and games she had.
question_hinglish: Akhila ke Hoopla games uski Giant Wheel rides ke aadhe hain. Ek ride ₹3 ki aur ek Hoopla game ₹4 ka hai, aur usne ₹20 kharch kiye. Equations banao aur batao kitni rides aur games hue.
answer_english:
Let x = rides and y = Hoopla games.
y = x/2 …(1)
3x + 4y = 20 …(2)
Substitute (1) in (2): 3x + 4(x/2) = 20 → 5x = 20 → x = 4, y = 2.
She had 4 rides and played Hoopla 2 times. Jaanch: 3(4) + 4(2) = 20.

question_english: What are consistent, inconsistent and dependent pairs of linear equations? How do they relate to the graphs of the lines?
question_hinglish: Linear equations ki consistent, inconsistent aur dependent jodi kya hai? Inka lines ke graph se kya sambandh hai?
answer_english:
Consistent pair: has at least one solution.
Inconsistent pair: has no solution.
Dependent pair: the equations are equivalent and have infinitely many common solutions; a dependent pair is always consistent.
Graphically:
(i) lines intersect at one point → unique solution (consistent);
(ii) lines are parallel → no solution (inconsistent);
(iii) lines coincide → infinitely many solutions (dependent, consistent).
answer_hinglish:
Consistent jodi: kam se kam ek solution hota hai.
Inconsistent jodi: koi solution nahi.
Dependent jodi: equations barabar (equivalent) hain aur anginat common solutions hain; dependent jodi hamesha consistent hoti hai.
Graph se:
(i) lines ek point pe kaatein → unique solution (consistent);
(ii) lines parallel → koi solution nahi (inconsistent);
(iii) lines coincident → anginat solutions (dependent, consistent).
ncert_context: A pair of linear equations which has no solution, is called an inconsistent pair of linear equations. A pair of linear equations in two variables, which has a solution, is called a consistent pair of linear equations. A pair of linear equations which are equivalent has infinitely many distinct common solutions. Such a pair is called a dependent pair of linear equations in two variables. Note that a dependent pair of linear equations is always consistent. (i) the lines may intersect in a single point. In this case, the pair of equations has a unique solution (consistent pair of equations). (ii) the lines may be parallel. In this case, the equations have no solution (inconsistent pair of equations). (iii) the lines may be coincident. In this case, the equations have infinitely many solutions [dependent (consistent) pair of equations].

question_english: Use the ratios a₁/a₂, b₁/b₂, c₁/c₂ to classify these pairs: x − 2y = 0 & 3x + 4y − 20 = 0; 2x + 3y − 9 = 0 & 4x + 6y − 18 = 0; x + 2y − 4 = 0 & 2x + 4y − 12 = 0.
question_hinglish: Ratios a₁/a₂, b₁/b₂, c₁/c₂ se in jodiyon ko classify karo: x − 2y = 0 aur 3x + 4y − 20 = 0; 2x + 3y − 9 = 0 aur 4x + 6y − 18 = 0; x + 2y − 4 = 0 aur 2x + 4y − 12 = 0.
answer_english:
(1) 1/3 vs −2/4: a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂ → intersecting lines, exactly one solution.
(2) 2/4 = 3/6 = −9/−18 = 1/2 → coincident lines, infinitely many solutions.
(3) 1/2 = 2/4 = 1/2 but −4/−12 = 1/3 → parallel lines, no solution.
Rule: intersecting if a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂; coincident if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂; parallel if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂. The converses also hold.

(3) 1/2 = 2/4 = 1/2 par −4/−12 = 1/3 → parallel lines, koi solution nahi.
Niyam: kaatti agar a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂; coincident agar a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂; parallel agar a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂. Converses bhi sahi hain.

question_english: Are these pairs consistent or inconsistent? (i) 3x + 2y = 5; 2x − 3y = 7 (ii) 2x − 3y = 8; 4x − 6y = 9 (iii) (3/2)x + (5/3)y = 7; 9x − 10y = 14 (iv) 5x − 3y = 11; −10x + 6y = −22 (v) (4/3)x + 2y = 8; 2x + 3y = 12
question_hinglish: Ye jodiyan consistent hain ya inconsistent? (i) 3x + 2y = 5; 2x − 3y = 7 (ii) 2x − 3y = 8; 4x − 6y = 9 (iii) (3/2)x + (5/3)y = 7; 9x − 10y = 14 (iv) 5x − 3y = 11; −10x + 6y = −22 (v) (4/3)x + 2y = 8; 2x + 3y = 12
answer_english:
(i) 3/2 ≠ 2/(−3) → consistent (unique solution).
(ii) 2/4 = −3/−6 = 1/2 but 8/9 ≠ 1/2 → inconsistent (parallel).

(v) (4/3)/2 = 2/3, 2/3 = 2/3, 8/12 = 2/3 → dependent, consistent.

x − y + 1 = 0 passes through (−1, 0) and (0, 1); it meets the x-axis at (−1, 0).
3x + 2y − 12 = 0 passes through (4, 0) and (0, 6); it meets the x-axis at (4, 0).
Intersection: y = x + 1 → 3x + 2x + 2 = 12 → x = 2, y = 3, i.e. (2, 3).
Vertices of the triangle: (−1, 0), (4, 0) and (2, 3).

chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
question_english: List the steps of the substitution method. What does it mean if you get a statement with no variable?
question_hinglish: Substitution method ke steps batao. Agar aisa statement mile jisme koi variable na ho toh iska kya matlab hai?
answer_english:
Step 1: from either equation, express one variable (say y) in terms of the other (x), whichever is convenient.
Step 2: substitute it in the other equation to get an equation in one variable, and solve it.
Step 3: substitute this value back into the equation from Step 1 to find the other variable.
If Step 2 gives a statement with no variable: if it is true (e.g. 18 = 18), the pair has infinitely many solutions; if it is false (e.g. −4 = 0), the pair is inconsistent (no solution).
answer_hinglish:
Step 1: kisi bhi equation se ek variable (maano y) ko doosre (x) ke roop mein likho, jo aasaan ho.
Step 2: ise doosri equation mein daalo, ek variable ki equation milegi, use hal karo.
Step 3: ye value Step 1 waali equation mein wapas daalkar doosra variable nikaalo.
Agar Step 2 mein bina variable ka statement mile: sahi ho (jaise 18 = 18) toh jodi ke anginat solutions hain; galat ho (jaise −4 = 0) toh jodi inconsistent hai (koi solution nahi).
ncert_context: Step 1: Find the value of one variable, say y in terms of the other variable, i.e., x from either equation, whichever is convenient. Step 2: Substitute this value of y in the other equation, and reduce it to an equation in one variable, i.e., in terms of x, which can be solved. Sometimes, as in Examples 9 and 10 below, you can get statements with no variable. If this statement is true, you can conclude that the pair of linear equations has infinitely many solutions. If the statement is false, then the pair of linear equations is inconsistent. Step 3: Substitute the value of x (or y) obtained in Step 2 in the equation used in Step 1 to obtain the value of the other variable. We have substituted the value of one variable by expressing it in terms of the other variable to solve the pair of linear equations. That is why the method is known as the substitution method.

question_english: Aftab tells his daughter: 'Seven years ago I was seven times as old as you; three years from now I shall be three times as old as you.' Find their present ages by substitution.
question_hinglish: Aftab apni beti se kehta hai: 'Saat saal pehle main tumse saat guna bada tha; teen saal baad main tumse teen guna bada hounga.' Substitution se dono ki abhi ki umar nikaalo.
answer_english:
Let Aftab = s and daughter = t years.
s − 7 = 7(t − 7) → s − 7t + 42 = 0 …(1)
s + 3 = 3(t + 3) → s − 3t = 6 …(2)
From (2): s = 3t + 6. Substitute in (1): 3t + 6 − 7t + 42 = 0 → 4t = 48 → t = 12; s = 42.
Aftab is 42 and his daughter 12. Jaanch: 35 = 7 × 5 and 45 = 3 × 15.
answer_hinglish:
Aftab = s aur beti = t saal maano.
s − 7 = 7(t − 7) → s − 7t + 42 = 0 …(1)
s + 3 = 3(t + 3) → s − 3t = 6 …(2)
(2) se: s = 3t + 6. (1) mein daalo: 3t + 6 − 7t + 42 = 0 → 4t = 48 → t = 12; s = 42.
Aftab 42 aur beti 12 saal ki hai. Jaanch: 35 = 7 × 5 aur 45 = 3 × 15.
ncert_context: Example 5: Aftab tells his daughter, 'Seven years ago, I was seven times as old as you were then. Also, three years from now, I shall be three times as old as you will be.' Represent this situation algebraically and graphically by the method of substitution. Let s and t be the ages (in years) of Aftab and his daughter, respectively. Then, the pair of linear equations that represent the situation is s – 7 = 7(t – 7), i.e., s – 7t + 42 = 0 (1) and s + 3 = 3(t + 3), i.e., s – 3t = 6 (2). Using Equation (2), we get s = 3t + 6. Putting this value of s in Equation (1), we get (3t + 6) – 7t + 42 = 0, i.e., 4t = 48, which gives t = 12. Putting this value of t in Equation (2), we get s = 3(12) + 6 = 42. So, Aftab and his daughter are 42 and 12 years old, respectively.

question_english: (a) 2 pencils and 3 erasers cost ₹9, and 4 pencils and 6 erasers cost ₹18. Can a unique price be found? (b) Two rails are x + 2y − 4 = 0 and 2x + 4y − 12 = 0. Will they cross?
question_hinglish: (a) 2 pencil aur 3 rubber ₹9 ke, aur 4 pencil aur 6 rubber ₹18 ke hain. Kya unique keemat nikal sakti hai? (b) Do patriyan x + 2y − 4 = 0 aur 2x + 4y − 12 = 0 hain. Kya ye kaategi?
answer_english:
(a) From 2x + 3y = 9, x = (9 − 3y)/2. Substitute in 4x + 6y = 18: 18 − 6y + 6y = 18 → 18 = 18, true for all y. The equations are the same, so there are infinitely many solutions and no unique price.
(b) From x + 2y − 4 = 0, x = 4 − 2y. Substitute: 2(4 − 2y) + 4y − 12 = 0 → −4 = 0, a false statement. No common solution, so the lines are parallel and the rails will not cross.
answer_hinglish:
(a) 2x + 3y = 9 se x = (9 − 3y)/2. 4x + 6y = 18 mein daalo: 18 − 6y + 6y = 18 → 18 = 18, har y ke liye sahi. Equations same hain, toh anginat solutions hain aur koi unique keemat nahi.
(b) x + 2y − 4 = 0 se x = 4 − 2y. Daalo: 2(4 − 2y) + 4y − 12 = 0 → −4 = 0, galat statement. Koi common solution nahi, toh lines parallel hain aur patriyan nahi kaategi.

This statement is true for all values of y. Both the given equations are the same. Therefore, Equations (1) and (2) have infinitely many solutions. We cannot find a unique cost of a pencil and an eraser. Example 7: Two rails are represented by the equations x + 2y – 4 = 0 and 2x + 4y – 12 = 0. So, the two rails will not cross each other.

question_hinglish: Substitution se hal karo: (i) x + y = 14, x − y = 4; (ii) s − t = 3, s/3 + t/2 = 6; (iii) 0.2x + 0.3y = 1.3, 0.4x + 0.5y = 2.3; (iv) 3x − y = 3, 9x − 3y = 9.
answer_english:
(i) x = 14 − y → 14 − 2y = 4 → y = 5, x = 9.
(ii) s = t + 3; 2s + 3t = 36 → 2t + 6 + 3t = 36 → t = 6, s = 9.
(iii) Multiply by 10: 2x + 3y = 13, 4x + 5y = 23. x = (13 − 3y)/2 → 26 − 6y + 5y = 23 → y = 3, x = 2.
(iv) y = 3x − 3 → 9x − 9x + 9 = 9 → 9 = 9, always true: infinitely many solutions (the second equation is 3 × the first).
answer_hinglish:
Ek variable ko doosre ke roop mein likhkar daalo:

question_english: The sum of a two-digit number and its reverse is 66 and the digits differ by 2. Using elimination, find all such numbers.
question_hinglish: Do-ank number aur uske ulte ka jod 66 hai aur ankon ka fark 2 hai. Elimination se aise saare numbers nikaalo.
answer_english:
Tens digit x, units digit y: (10x + y) + (10y + x) = 66 → x + y = 6.
Digits differ by 2: either x − y = 2 or y − x = 2.
Case 1: x + y = 6, x − y = 2 → x = 4, y = 2 → 42.
Case 2: x + y = 6, y − x = 2 → x = 2, y = 4 → 24.
There are two such numbers, 42 and 24 (42 + 24 = 66).

question_english: Why are algebraic methods often preferred over the graphical method? Compare substitution and elimination.
question_hinglish: Graphical method ki jagah algebraic methods aksar kyun pasand kiye jaate hain? Substitution aur elimination ki tulna karo.
answer_english:
The graphical method is inconvenient when the solution has non-integral coordinates like (√3, 2√7), (−1.75, 3.3) or (4/13, 1/19); reading such points from a graph easily leads to mistakes. Algebraic methods give exact answers.
Substitution: express one variable in terms of the other from one equation and substitute into the other. Convenient when a variable has coefficient 1.
Elimination: multiply the equations to make one variable's coefficients equal, then add or subtract to remove it. Often more convenient when coefficients are larger. Both detect no-solution and infinite-solution cases through false or true variable-free statements.
answer_hinglish:
Graphical method tab mushkil hai jab solution ke coordinates poore number na hon, jaise (√3, 2√7), (−1.75, 3.3) ya (4/13, 1/19); graph se aise points padhne mein galti ho jaati hai. Algebraic methods sateek jawab dete hain.
Substitution: ek equation se ek variable ko doosre ke roop mein likhkar doosri mein daalo. Jab kisi variable ka coefficient 1 ho tab aasaan.
Elimination: equations ko guna karke ek variable ke coefficients barabar karo, phir jodkar ya ghataakar use hatao. Bade coefficients mein aksar aasaan. Dono bina variable ke galat ya sahi statement se 'koi solution nahi' ya 'anginat solutions' pakad lete hain.
ncert_context: The graphical method is not convenient in cases when the point representing the solution of the linear equations has non-integral coordinates like (√3, 2√7), (–1.75, 3.3), (4/13, 1/19), etc. There is every possibility of making mistakes while reading such coordinates. Is there any alternative method of finding the solution? There are several algebraic methods. We have substituted the value of one variable by expressing it in terms of the other variable to solve the pair of linear equations. That is why the method is known as the substitution method. Now let us consider another method of eliminating (i.e., removing) one variable. This is sometimes more convenient than the substitution method. The method is called the elimination method, because we eliminate one variable first, to get a linear equation in one variable.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: What is a quadratic equation? What is its standard form?
question_hinglish: Quadratic equation kya hoti hai? Iska standard form kya hai?
answer_english:
A quadratic equation in the variable x is an equation of the form ax² + bx + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a ≠ 0.
Any equation p(x) = 0 where p(x) is a polynomial of degree 2 is a quadratic equation. Writing the terms in descending order of degree gives the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0, a ≠ 0.
Examples: 2x² + x − 300 = 0, 2x² − 3x + 1 = 0, 4x − 3x² + 2 = 0.
answer_hinglish:

Koi bhi equation p(x) = 0 jahan p(x) degree 2 ka polynomial ho, quadratic equation hai. Terms ko degree ke ghatte kram mein likhne pe standard form ax² + bx + c = 0, a ≠ 0 milta hai.
Udaharan: 2x² + x − 300 = 0, 2x² − 3x + 1 = 0, 4x − 3x² + 2 = 0.
ncert_context: A quadratic equation in the variable x is an equation of the form ax² + bx + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers, a ≠ 0. For example, 2x² + x – 300 = 0 is a quadratic equation. Similarly, 2x² – 3x + 1 = 0, 4x – 3x² + 2 = 0 and 1 – x² + 300 = 0 are also quadratic equations. In fact, any equation of the form p(x) = 0, where p(x) is a polynomial of degree 2, is a quadratic equation. But when we write the terms of p(x) in descending order of their degrees, then we get the standard form of the equation. That is, ax² + bx + c = 0, a ≠ 0 is called the standard form of a quadratic equation.

subject: Mathematics
question_english: Who contributed to solving quadratic equations historically?
question_hinglish: Itihaas mein quadratic equations hal karne mein kiska yogdaan raha?
answer_english:
Babylonians are believed to be the first; they could find two positive numbers with a given sum and product (equivalent to x² − px + q = 0).
Euclid developed a geometrical approach.
Brahmagupta (C.E. 598–665) gave an explicit formula for ax² + bx = c.
Sridharacharya (C.E. 1025) derived the quadratic formula by completing the square (as quoted by Bhaskara II).
Al-Khwarizmi (about C.E. 800) studied different types, and Abraham bar Hiyya Ha-Nasi's 'Liber embadorum' (C.E. 1145) gave complete solutions.
answer_hinglish:
Maana jaata hai Babylonians sabse pehle the; woh diye gaye jod aur guna waale do positive numbers nikaal lete the (jo x² − px + q = 0 ke barabar hai).
Euclid ne geometrical tareeka banaya.
Brahmagupta (C.E. 598–665) ne ax² + bx = c ke liye spasht formula diya.
Sridharacharya (C.E. 1025) ne completing the square se quadratic formula nikaala (Bhaskara II ke anusaar).
Al-Khwarizmi (lagbhag C.E. 800) ne alag prakaar padhe, aur Abraham bar Hiyya Ha-Nasi ki 'Liber embadorum' (C.E. 1145) ne poore solutions diye.
